title: How to win the Amazon Buy Box in 2026
excerpt: The pricing, fulfillment and account-health signals that decide who owns the Buy Box.
body: The Amazon Buy Box accounts for the vast majority of sales on any listing — if you don't own it, your offer is effectively invisible. Winning it consistently in 2026 comes down to a handful of signals Amazon weighs on every single page view.
## Price competitively, not desperately

Amazon rewards a fair landed price — item plus shipping — not simply the lowest number. Race-to-the-bottom pricing erodes your margin without guaranteeing the box. We set rule-based repricing with a floor that protects profit and still reacts to competitors in near real time.
## Fulfillment is your biggest lever

Prime-eligible offers through FBA or Seller-Fulfilled Prime win the Buy Box far more often than standard fulfillment. A fast, reliable delivery promise carries more weight with the algorithm than a few cents of price difference ever will.
## Protect your account health

A strong Order Defect Rate, low late-shipment and cancellation rates, and healthy inventory all feed Buy Box eligibility. A single account-health issue can quietly drop you out of the box across your entire catalog.
The signals we monitor daily:
- Landed price versus the competition
- Prime eligibility and delivery speed
- Seller metrics: ODR, late-shipment and cancellation rates
- Inventory depth and restock timing
## The takeaway
The Buy Box isn't won once — it's defended every day. We manage pricing, fulfillment and account health together so your listings stay in the box and keep converting.

title: TikTok Shop: a launch checklist for new brands
excerpt: Everything you need to set up Shop, connect creators and run your first LIVE.
body: TikTok Shop has become one of the fastest routes from discovery to checkout — but a rushed launch leaves sales on the table. Here's the checklist we run for every new brand we onboard.
## 1. Set up Shop correctly

Verify your business, connect your account, and configure shipping templates, returns and payments before you list a single product. Getting compliance right up front avoids holds and headaches later.
## 2. Get your catalog live and optimized
Sync your catalog, write short-form-friendly titles, and lead with video. Products that show well in a vertical 9:16 frame convert far better than flat, catalog-style photos.
## 3. Turn on creators and affiliates
TikTok Shop is a creator engine. Open your affiliate program, set commissions that are genuinely worth a creator's time, and seed product to a focused shortlist of creators in your niche.
## 4. Go LIVE
Schedule regular LIVE shopping sessions and pair them with Spark Ads to amplify what's already working. Early on, consistency beats production value every time.
Your first-week checklist:
- Business verification complete
- Catalog synced with video-first listings
- Affiliate program open with sensible commissions
- First LIVE scheduled and promoted
Do these four things well and you'll have a Shop that's ready to scale — not just switched on.

title: Etsy SEO: ranking your listings the right way
excerpt: How tags, titles and attributes work together inside the Etsy search algorithm.
body: Etsy SEO rewards relevance and quality together. Stuffing keywords won't save a listing that buyers scroll past — but the right tags, titles and attributes put you in front of shoppers who are ready to buy.
## How Etsy search actually works

Etsy first matches a query to your listing using titles, tags, categories and attributes, then ranks the matches with a quality score built from clicks, favorites and conversions. Relevance gets you into the race; quality is what wins it.
## Titles, tags and attributes work together
Use all thirteen tags with multi-word phrases your buyers actually search, mirror those phrases in the first few words of your title, and complete every attribute — they double as hidden tags.
Where to focus first:
- Thirteen long-tail tags — never single words
- Front-load the title with your strongest phrase
- Complete every category and attribute
- Match your listing photos to the search intent
## Beyond keywords: quality signals

Great photography, competitive shipping (free-shipping thresholds help), strong reviews and a healthy conversion rate all lift your ranking over time. SEO opens the door; the listing experience keeps it open.
Treat Etsy SEO as ongoing maintenance rather than a one-time setup, and your best listings will compound visibility month after month.

title: How to Put Your eBay Store on Vacation [2026 Guide]
excerpt: Going away or need a break? Here’s how to put your eBay store on vacation, what to sort out before you leave, and how to switch it back on.
body: eBay now calls its vacation mode feature Time Away. To put your eBay store on vacation, you need to go to My eBay, then Account settings, then Time Away settings.

After that, select Schedule time away, choose Allow item sales or Pause item sales, set your start and end dates, and select Apply. You can pause sales for up to 30 days, or keep selling with later delivery dates for up to 15 days.
The right option depends on whether you can still process orders during your break.
In this guide, you’ll learn how both options work and what you should check before leaving.

**And if you'd rather have someone handle your eBay store while you're away,** [**Alpha Digital Solutions**](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/) **can help with day-to-day store management, so you can take a break without worrying about every little task.**
## What Is eBay Time Away?

eBay's **Time Away** is eBay's version of vacation mode. It is a built-in seller tool that basically lets you temporarily pause your listings or adjust delivery expectations. You can use this feature when you are away, sick, or need a break without shutting down your store.
You can choose between two options:

- **Allow item sales:** Your listings stay visible, and buyers can continue purchasing. eBay displays a message telling buyers you're away and adjusts estimated delivery dates for most eligible listings.
- **Pause item sales:** Your fixed-price listings are hidden from search results, and buyers cannot purchase them while you're away.
Time Away is available to all eBay sellers, not just those with an eBay Store subscription.
It's worth knowing that these options have different time limits. You can allow sales to continue for up to 15 days or pause sales for up to 30 days.
## What Happened To eBay Vacation Mode?

Lots of sellers still search for "vacation mode" or "put store on vacation eBay". eBay has replaced its traditional vacation mode with Time Away. The old vacation settings were once limited to eBay Store subscribers, but Time Away is now available to every seller.
Remember that eBay store subscriptions and listing fees continue to apply while you are away.
## How To Put Your eBay Store On Vacation, Step By Step
Here's how to put an eBay store on vacation using Time Away:
## Step 1: Go to Time Away Settings
First, log in to your eBay seller account.
Go to **My eBay > Account settings > Time Away settings**. You can also access Time Away through Seller Hub under Selling tools.
Make sure you're signed into the account where you want to schedule the break.
## Step 2: Select Schedule Time Away
Once you're on the Time Away page, click **Schedule time away**.
eBay will ask whether you want to allow item sales or pause them while you're away. Both options work differently, so it's worth understanding them before making a choice.
## Step 3: Choose Whether to Allow or Pause Sales
You'll see two options:
**Allow item sales**
Choose this if you want buyers to keep purchasing your products while you're away.

Your listings will remain visible, and eBay will show buyers a message explaining that you're on Time Away. For most eligible listings, eBay will also adjust the estimated delivery dates automatically.
You can use this option for up to 15 days.
**Pause item sales**
Choose this if you don't want to receive new orders during your break.
Your fixed-price listings will be hidden from search results, and buyers won't be able to purchase them while Time Away is active.
However, auction-style listings will remain visible and available for purchase. Buyers will see a message that you're away.
You can pause item sales for up to 30 days.
## Step 4: Set Your Start and End Dates
After choosing your preferred option, select the dates for your break.
- **Start date:** The day you want Time Away to begin.
- **End date:** The last day you want it to remain active.
If you schedule it in advance, Time Away starts at 12:01 AM on your selected start date and ends at 11:59 PM on your selected end date.

One useful tip: eBay recommends starting Time Away a day before your actual break and ending it a day after you return. This gives you some extra time to handle last-minute orders and pending deliveries.
## Step 5: Select Apply
Once you've checked your settings and dates, click **Apply**.
That's it! Your Time Away schedule is set.

Keep in mind that if you start Time Away immediately, it can take a few hours for delivery dates to update or fixed-price listings to disappear from search results. So don't assume everything changes instantly.
## Which Option Should You Pick To Put Your eBay Store On Vacation?
If you're away for a few days and can ship when you're back, allow item sales to keep money coming in. If you can't ship anything, or you're away for more than 15 days, pause item sales.
## What To Check Before Putting Your eBay Store On Vacation
Before you leave, it's worth checking a few things to avoid problems while you're away.
Spend ten minutes on this checklist before you put your eBay store on vacation.
- Schedule Time Away ahead of time. It can take a few hours for fixed-price listings to be hidden, so don't leave it until you're heading out the door.
- Check your auctions and end any that finish while you're away.
- Be careful with offers. eBay doesn't update delivery dates for Second Chance Offers, auto-accepted offers, pending counteroffers, or seller-initiated offers accepted during Time Away.
- Check any items with local pickup or digital delivery, since eBay doesn't adjust delivery dates on those either.
- Review your Promoted Listings campaigns, so you aren't paying for ads on items that can't sell while you're gone.
- Ship everything you can before you leave.

If you'd rather not pause your store at all, there's another option. A dedicated person can keep listings, messages and orders moving while you're away. That's exactly what our [eBay account management](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/services/ebay) service is for.
## How To Turn Off eBay Vacation Mode When You Return
Once you're ready to start selling again, you don't need to recreate your listings or manually make them visible.
If you've scheduled an end date, Time Away will end automatically.
Your fixed-price listings will gradually return to search results if you selected Pause item sales. This can take a few hours, so don't worry if they don't appear immediately.
**Want to end Time Away early?** Follow these steps:
- Go to your eBay Time Away settings.
- Select **Cancel time away** or change the end date to an earlier date.
- Select **Apply**.
That's all you need to do. Your listings will gradually become available again, although it may take a couple of hours for them to reappear in search results.
Once you're back, check your messages, orders and any pending buyer requests so nothing gets missed.
## Frequently Asked Questions
## 1. Can I put my eBay store on vacation for 30 days?
Yes. You can pause item sales for up to 30 days using Time Away. If you want to keep accepting orders while you're away, the maximum period is 15 days.
## 2. Can buyers still purchase my products when my eBay store is on vacation?

It depends on the option you select. If you choose Allow item sales, buyers can continue purchasing your products. If you choose Pause item sales, fixed-price listings are hidden from search and cannot be purchased. Auction-style listings remain available.
## 3. Does eBay vacation mode affect my existing listings?
Your listings aren't deleted when you use Time Away. If you pause sales, your fixed-price listings are temporarily hidden and automatically return to search results when Time Away ends.
## 4. Can I put my eBay store on vacation without an eBay Store subscription?
Yes. Time Away is available to all eBay sellers, including those who don't have an eBay Store subscription.
## 5. Do I need to change my handling time manually?

Usually not. If you select Allow item sales, eBay automatically adjusts estimated delivery dates for most eligible listings. However, some listing types and transactions are excluded, so check those separately.
## Taking a Break From Selling? Let Alpha Digital Help
Managing an eBay store takes time, even when you're not actively selling. Between updating listings, handling orders and responding to buyers, there's always something that needs attention.
If you need help keeping your store running, Alpha Digital can assist with eBay account management, from product listings to day-to-day store operations.
Explore our [eBay account management](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/services/ebay) services or [book a call](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/contact) with our team to discuss your requirements.
## Final Thoughts

Taking a break from eBay doesn't have to mean shutting down your business completely. With Time Away, you can either keep accepting orders with adjusted delivery dates or pause your fixed-price listings until you're ready to return.
Just choose the option that works for your situation, set your dates carefully and take care of any pending orders before leaving.
That way, you can enjoy your time off without worrying about what might be happening in your eBay store.

title: eBay Store Subscription: Is It Worth It?
excerpt: Is an eBay Store subscription worth the monthly fee? Here are the current plans and prices, who each one suits, how to get a discount, and how to cancel.
body: ## eBay Store Subscription: Is It Worth It?

An eBay Store subscription costs between $4.95 and $2,999.95 a month on eBay.com, depending on the plan and whether you pay yearly or monthly. For most small and growing sellers, the plan to look at is Basic, which is $21.95 a month on a yearly plan or $27.95 on a monthly plan. It's usually worth it once you list enough items to use the extra free listings and the lower fees.
You can cancel from your subscription page, but cancelling a yearly plan early can cost you a fee.
In this guide, you'll learn what each plan costs, how to decide if a Store pays off for you, and how to cancel your eBay store subscription.
And if you'd rather have someone set up and run your store for you,[Alpha Digital Solutions](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/services/ebay) can help.
## eBay Store Subscription Tiers and Prices
eBay Stores come in five levels. These are the prices on eBay.com in the US. Other eBay sites, including eBay UK, have their own plans and prices, so check yours before you decide.
- **Starter:** $4.95 a month on a yearly plan, or $7.95 on a monthly plan. You get 250 free listings a month, then pay $0.30 for each extra listing.
- **Basic:** $21.95 yearly, or $27.95 monthly. You get 1,000 free fixed-price listings a month, then pay $0.25 for each extra listing.
- **Premium:** $59.95 yearly, or $74.95 monthly. You get 10,000 free fixed-price listings, then pay $0.10 for each extra listing.
- **Anchor:** $299.95 yearly, or $349.95 monthly. You get 25,000 free fixed-price listings, then pay $0.05 for each extra listing.
- **Enterprise:** $2,999.95 a month, on a yearly plan only. You get 100,000 free fixed-price listings, then pay $0.05 for each extra listing.
Whichever plan you pick, eBay charges the subscription fee every month. A yearly plan is cheaper per month, but it's a one-year commitment, which matters if you cancel early (more on that below).
## Is An eBay Store Subscription Worth It?

The honest answer is that it depends on how much you list and sell. A Store gives you more free listings each month, discounted fees, a branded storefront and extra tools to promote your business. Those perks only help if you actually use them.
A Store is probably worth a look if:
- You list hundreds of items a month or more, so you keep running past your free listings.
- You sell steadily, so the lower fees add up month after month.
- You want a branded storefront and tools like promotions and coupons.
You can probably wait if:
- You only list a small number of items.
- Your sales are slow or very seasonal.
- You aren't sure eBay will be a long-term channel for you.

Here's a quick way to check. Add up how many listings you create or renew in a typical month, and what you pay in listing and selling fees. Then compare that with the monthly cost of Basic. If the savings and the extra free listings clearly beat the subscription, it's worth it. If they don't, hold off. Check eBay's current fee page for your category, since fees can vary.
Starter is the cheapest way to have a Store, but its free listing allowance is much the same as what you'd get without one. It mostly suits sellers who mainly want the storefront.
## How To Get An eBay Store Subscription Discount
There's no single discount code that works for everyone, but there are a few real ways to pay less.
- **Choose a yearly plan.** It costs less each month than a monthly plan. For example, Basic is $21.95 instead of $27.95. Just be sure you're happy to commit for the year.

- **Watch for eBay offers.** eBay runs occasional promotions, such as a few months at a lower rate when you subscribe or upgrade. They usually arrive by email or as a message in My eBay Messages, and you often have to click Accept offer to get them. They change, and some only apply to certain sellers or to eBay.com.
- **Use the perks.** Higher plans include extras, such as a quarterly coupon for eBay-branded shipping supplies, which can help offset the cost.
Be careful with websites that sell "eBay Store discount codes". If an offer isn't in your own eBay account, treat it with caution.
## Is an Annual eBay Subscription Discount Worth It?
If you're comparing subscription costs, you'll notice that eBay's annual renewal option is cheaper than its monthly renewal option.
For example, a Basic Store costs $27.95 per month with monthly renewal, compared with $21.95 per month on a yearly plan.
That's a difference of $6 per month, or $72 over 12 months at the published rates.
However, an annual subscription comes with a one-year commitment. Cancelling or downgrading before the commitment period ends may result in an early termination fee.
Before choosing the annual option, consider:
- How consistently you sell on eBay.
- Whether your current inventory justifies a paid subscription.
- Whether you expect to maintain your store throughout the year.
- Whether the potential savings outweigh the commitment.
If you're still testing your products or sales volume, monthly renewal may offer more flexibility.
## How To Cancel Your eBay Store Subscription
Here's how to do it:
- Go to Seller Hub, then the Store tab, then Manage subscription. Or go to My eBay, then Account, then Subscriptions.
- Find your active Store subscription and select Cancel subscription.
- Review the details and submit.
Before cancelling, keep a few things in mind:
- If you're on an annual plan, an early termination fee may apply.
- Your current auction-style listings can remain active until they end or sell.
- Active fixed-price listings may become subject to standard selling fees after your Store closes.
- Your Store subscription benefits will stop applying from the first day of the month after cancellation.
If you only need a break, you don't have to close your Store. You can[put your eBay Store on vacation](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/blog/how-to-put-your-ebay-store-on-vacation-2026-guide) instead.
## Frequently Asked Questions
## How much is an eBay Store subscription?
On eBay.com, it ranges from $4.95 a month (Starter, yearly plan) to $2,999.95 a month (Enterprise). Basic is $21.95 on a yearly plan or $27.95 monthly.
## Can I change my eBay Store subscription level?
Yes. You can upgrade or downgrade your subscription based on your business needs. However, check the applicable billing and early termination terms, particularly if you're on a yearly plan.
## Can I cancel my eBay Store subscription at any time?
You can request cancellation through your account's subscription settings. However, annual subscriptions may involve early termination fees if cancelled before the commitment period ends.
## Does an eBay Store subscription eliminate selling fees?
No. A subscription provides certain listing allowances and fee benefits, but sellers may still be charged applicable insertion fees, final value fees and optional listing upgrade fees.
## Do I need an eBay Store to sell on eBay?
No. A Store adds more free listings, discounted fees and extra tools, but you can sell without one.
## Want Help Deciding? Let Alpha Digital Solutions Help

Choosing the right plan is easier when someone looks at your actual numbers. If you'd like a second pair of eyes on your store, or you want it set up and managed for you,[book a free consultation](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/contact) and we'll go through it with you.
## Final Thoughts
An eBay Store isn’t a must-have, and it isn’t a waste either. It’s a tool that pays off when you list and sell enough to use what it gives you.
Start by checking your own numbers, pick the plan that fits where your business is today, and remember you can change it later.
If your sales grow, you can upgrade. And if you’re not sure yet, there’s no harm in waiting.

title: Ecommerce SEO Strategy: 9 Steps to Boost Traffic
excerpt: Learn how to build an ecommerce SEO strategy that brings more buyers to your store. A simple step-by-step guide covering technical SEO, keywords, product pages and links.
body: A successful ecommerce SEO strategy makes your product catalogue easy for search engines to crawl and aligns your pages with commercial buyer intent.
This guide walks through the steps we follow when we plan SEO for an online store.
You can use these steps to build your own ecommerce SEO strategy or to check whether the one you already have makes sense.
## Ecommerce SEO Strategy: Step-by-Step
Here are nine steps to build an ecommerce strategy that can bring steady organic traffic and real orders to your store.
## Step 1: Fix the Technical Basics First
Before you touch keywords or content, make sure Google can crawl and index your store properly. This is the base of any ecommerce SEO strategy.
Open Google Search Console and look for these problems:
- Pages that are not indexed
- Slow pages and poor mobile experience
- Duplicate URLs created by filters and product variants
- Broken links and redirect chains
Many stores have hundreds of junk URLs that waste Google's attention. Clean those up first, because everything else depends on it.

If you want a deeper look at this side of things, our [SEO services for ecommerce](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/services/seo-services-for-ecommerce) help fix technical issues and bring more relevant shoppers to your store.
## Step 2: Do Keyword Research for Each Page Type
Different pages need different keywords.
- **Category pages** target broader searches, like "women's running shoes".
- **Product pages** target specific searches, like a product name or model.
- **Blog posts** target questions, like "how to choose running shoes".
Make a simple sheet with one main keyword for every page. This sheet becomes the backbone of your ecommerce SEO strategy.
Never give two pages the same main keyword, or they end up competing with each other.
For each keyword, check the search volume, the difficulty and what Google already shows. If the top results are all category pages, a blog post will not rank for it.
If your store is new, start with longer and less competitive keywords. Winning ten small searches is better than losing one big one.
## Step 3: Build a Clean Site Structure
Keep your structure simple: homepage, then categories, then subcategories, then products. Every page should be reachable within three clicks from the homepage.
Use short, readable URLs like /running-shoes/womens/ instead of long strings of numbers.
Also, link related categories and products to each other so shoppers and Google can move around easily.
## Step 4: Optimise Your Category Pages First
Category pages usually have more search volume than single products, and they are often easier to rank.
They are also where many buyers start their search.
For each important category, write a unique title and meta description, add a short intro with your main keyword, and include some helpful content like sizing tips or a quick buying guide.
Keep it short and useful. A huge block of text at the bottom of the page does not help anyone.
## Step 5: Optimise Your Product Pages
Product pages are where the sale happens, so they need to work for both Google and the buyer.
- Write your own product descriptions. Copying the supplier's text means you share the same content with every other store that sells the product.
- Put the product name and the most important detail in the title.
- Use clear photos with descriptive file names and alt text.
- Show customer reviews.
- Answer the common questions right on the page, like delivery time, returns and sizing.
For out of stock products, keep the page live if the item is coming back. If it is gone for good, redirect it to the closest category or product.
## Step 6: Add Structured Data

Structured data, also called schema, helps Google understand your products. With product schema, Google can show your price, stock status and star ratings right in the search results, which makes your listing stand out.
Add Product schema, Review schema and Breadcrumb schema to your store.
Then test your pages with Google's Rich Results Test to make sure it works.
On platforms like Shopify, many themes add some of this already, but it is worth checking that it is complete and correct.
## Step 7: Create Content That Supports Your Products
Blog posts will not sell your products directly, but they bring in shoppers who are still deciding.
Write buying guides, comparisons and how-to posts that answer the questions your customers ask.
Then link each post to the related category and product pages. That link is what turns a reader into a customer, and it also helps those pages rank.
## Step 8: Build Links to Your Store
Links from other websites are still one of the strongest signals for Google. Some realistic ways to get them for a store:
- Brands and suppliers that list stockists on their site
- Industry and local business directories
- Press mentions and product reviews
- Guest posts on blogs your customers read
- Helpful content, like guides and tools, that people want to link to
A handful of relevant links is worth more than hundreds of poor ones.
## Step 9: Track What Matters
Set up Google Search Console and GA4, then check a few numbers every month:
- Organic traffic to your store
- Rankings for your main category keywords
- Orders and revenue from organic search
Look at the trend, not the daily ups and downs. SEO moves slowly, and checking every day only creates stress.
## How Long Does an Ecommerce SEO Strategy Take to Work?

Most stores see early movement in 3 to 4 months and clearer results in 6 to 12 months. Technical fixes can help faster. New content and links take longer to build. The age of your store and how competitive your products are also make a difference.

Then we put together a clear plan with the priorities, timeline and price agreed up front.
If you're looking to improve your store's organic visibility, [book a free consultation](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/contact) to discuss your website and goals.
## Frequently Asked Questions About Ecommerce SEO Strategy
## What is an ecommerce SEO strategy?

An ecommerce SEO strategy is a plan for getting your online store to rank higher on Google. It covers technical fixes, keyword research, category and product page optimisation, content and link building. The aim is to bring in more organic traffic that turns into sales.
## How do I create an ecommerce SEO strategy?

Start by fixing technical problems, then research keywords for each page type. Next, optimise your category and product pages, add structured data, create helpful content and build links. Track your organic traffic and sales each month so you can see what is working.
## What is the most important part of an ecommerce SEO strategy?

For most stores it is the category pages and the technical foundation. Category pages target the searches with the most volume, and technical problems can stop even good pages from ranking. Fix those two areas before you spend time on anything else.
## How is ecommerce SEO different from regular SEO?

Ecommerce SEO has to deal with thousands of product pages, filters, variants, out of stock items and duplicate descriptions. A normal business website usually has far fewer pages. That means ecommerce SEO needs more focus on site structure and page templates.
## How much does an ecommerce SEO strategy cost?

If you build it yourself, it costs your time and the price of a few tools. If you hire an agency, ecommerce SEO usually costs from a few hundred to a few thousand dollars a month, depending on the size of your store and how competitive your market is.
## Can I build an ecommerce SEO strategy myself?
Yes, if your store is small and you are comfortable learning the basics. Larger stores, or stores with technical problems, often need specialist help to avoid expensive mistakes.

title: The Complete Shopify SEO Checklist for 2026
excerpt: Want more organic sales from your Shopify store? Work through this Shopify SEO checklist to fix technical issues, improve your collection and product pages, speed up your store and rank higher on Google in 2026.
body: Shopify already handles a few things for you, like SSL, sitemaps and canonical tags. The rest is up to you: page titles, collection pages, speed, and content.
And that is where most stores lose traffic.
We have put together this practical **Shopify SEO checklist** based on what actually moves rankings for active stores in 2026.
You don't have to finish everything in one go. Some items take five minutes and some take a few hours, so tick them off as you go.

**If you would rather hand your store's growth to specialists, Alpha Digital Solutions provides full** [**SEO services for Shopify**](https://www.alphadigitalsol.com/services) **to handle the technical fixes, content, and ongoing optimisation for you.**
## Shopify SEO Checklist: Technical Basics
Nothing else works if Google can't find and index your pages. Use this Shopify SEO checklist to get your technical basics right.

- **Check your domain setup.** Shopify gives you free SSL, so your store should load on HTTPS. Set one primary domain in your settings, and Shopify will send visitors from your other domain versions to it.
- **Set up Google Search Console.** Verify your domain and submit your sitemap at yourstore.com/sitemap.xml. Shopify creates and updates the sitemap for you.
- **Set up GA4.** You need to see how much traffic and how many orders come from organic search.

- **Check the Pages report in Search Console.** Look at which pages are not indexed and why. Some are normal, like pages that redirect. Others, like important products that Google crawled but didn't index, need a closer look.
- **Fix broken links and 404 pages.** If you delete or move a product or collection, add a URL redirect to the closest relevant page so you don't lose its traffic.
- **Leave robots.txt alone** unless you know exactly why you are changing it. Shopify's default file works for most stores.
## Shopify SEO Checklist for Site Structure and URLs
A clean structure helps Google understand your store and helps shoppers find what they want.
- **Keep your structure simple.** Homepage, then collections, then products. Try to keep every product within three clicks of the homepage.
- **Put every product in at least one collection.** A product with no collection and no links pointing to it is hard for Google to find.

- **Use short, readable URL handles.** Something like /products/mens-leather-wallet works better than a long handle stuffed with keywords. Shopify's /products/, /collections/, /pages/ and /blogs/ prefixes are fixed and can't be removed, so don't spend time on them.
- **Create a redirect when you change a handle.** Shopify gives you a tick box for this when you edit a URL handle.

- **Link to the main product URL.** Shopify can show the same product under both /products/ and /collections/.../products/. It adds canonical tags so Google counts the main one, but when you add your own links in blog posts or emails, use the /products/ version.
- **Add breadcrumbs** if your theme doesn't show them. They help shoppers and give Google more context about where a page sits.
## Shopify SEO Checklist for Keyword Research

Before optimising product descriptions or writing blog posts, find out what your potential customers are searching for. Keyword research helps you understand the language shoppers use and which search terms are relevant to your products.
Use this Shopify SEO checklist to get your keyword research right.
- **Give every page one main keyword.** Never target the same keyword on two pages, or they end up competing with each other.

- **Match the keyword to the page type.** Collection pages go after broader searches, like "women's running shoes". Product pages go after specific ones, like a product name or model. Blog posts go after questions, like "how to choose running shoes".
- **Check what Google already shows.** If the top results for a keyword are all collection pages, a blog post probably won't rank for it.
- **Use your own data.** The Performance report in Google Search Console shows which searches already bring you impressions. Tools like Semrush or Ahrefs help you find new ideas.
- **Start small if your store is new.** Longer, less competitive keywords are easier to win than big head terms.
## Shopify SEO Checklist for Product Pages
Product pages are among the most important pages on an ecommerce store. They give shoppers the information they need to make a purchase and help search engines understand what you're selling.
A few keyword changes alone won't make a product page useful. You also need clear descriptions, accurate product information, and helpful images.
Follow these product page SEO checks:
- **Write your own product descriptions.** Copying the manufacturer's text means you share the same content with every other store selling that product.
- **Put the product name and key detail in the title tag.** Add a meta description that gives a reason to click.
- **Add alt text to every image.** Describe what is in the photo in plain words.
- **Show customer reviews.** They add fresh, useful content and help shoppers decide.
- **Answer common questions on the page.** Delivery times, returns and sizing are good places to start.
- **Use variants for sizes and colours** instead of making a separate product for each one, where it makes sense.
- **Handle out of stock items properly.** If a product is coming back, keep the page live. If it's gone for good, redirect it to the closest collection or product.
## Shopify SEO Checklist for Collection Pages
Collection pages organize your products into categories and help shoppers browse your store. They can also rank for broader searches that individual product pages may not target as effectively.
For example, a store selling home furniture might have separate collections for dining tables, office chairs, and bedroom furniture.
Here's what to check:
- **Choose descriptive collection names:** Use names that clearly explain what shoppers will find, such as "Women's Running Shoes" instead of vague labels like "Collection 1."
- **Optimize collection titles and meta descriptions:** Include relevant keywords while making each collection's purpose clear.
- **Add useful collection descriptions:** Explain what the category includes, what makes the products relevant, and what shoppers can expect.
- **Organize products logically:** Make it easy to browse products based on their type, features, or other useful categories.
- **Use descriptive collection images:** Choose images that represent the products in the collection.
- **Link to important collections:** Add links from your homepage, navigation menu, and relevant blog posts to help visitors and search engines discover them.
- **Avoid unnecessary collection duplication:** Don't create several collections with almost identical products and content just to target slightly different keywords.
## Shopify SEO Checklist for Speed and Core Web Vitals
Slow stores frustrate shoppers and can hold back rankings. Google measures this with Core Web Vitals.
- **Test your key pages in PageSpeed Insights.** Check your homepage, a top collection and a top product page.
- **Aim for the Core Web Vitals targets.** Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5 seconds, Interaction to Next Paint under 200 milliseconds and Cumulative Layout Shift under 0.1.
- **Review your apps.** Every app can add code that slows your store down. Remove the ones you don't use.
- **Check for leftover app code.** Uninstalling an app doesn't always remove the code it added to your theme, so ask your developer to check.
- **Upload sensibly sized images.** Shopify's CDN resizes images for you, but a huge original still makes pages heavier than they need to be.
- **Go easy on popups, sliders and videos** on your most important pages.
- **Use a modern, well-built theme.** Themes built on Online Store 2.0 are generally a good starting point.
## Shopify SEO Checklist for Content and Internal Links
Content brings in shoppers who are still deciding, and internal links help Google see how your pages connect.
- **Start a blog** that answers the questions your customers ask. Buying guides, comparisons and how-to posts work well.
- **Link every blog post to related collections and products.** That link is what turns a reader into a customer.
- **Link back from products and collections** to helpful guides where it makes sense.
- **Add an FAQ section** to important collection and product pages, with short, direct answers.
- **Update old posts** when something changes, instead of leaving them to go out of date.
## Shopify SEO Checklist for Links and Authority
Links from other websites are still one of the strongest signals for Google. For a store, realistic options include:
- Brands and suppliers that list stockists on their site
- Industry and local business directories
- Press mentions and product reviews
- Guest posts on blogs your customers read
- Guides and tools that people want to link to
A handful of relevant links is worth more than hundreds of poor ones. Avoid buying links.
Final Thoughts on Your Shopify SEO Checklist

You do not need to finish every item on this **Shopify SEO checklist** in a single afternoon. Start by fixing technical issues like duplicate URLs and slow app scripts, then work through your top-selling collections and product pages week by week.

## Frequently Asked Questions
## What SEO features does Shopify have built in?

Shopify includes free SSL, an automatically generated sitemap and robots.txt file, canonical tags and editable page titles, meta descriptions, image alt text and URL handles. It also lets you create URL redirects. You still need to fill in the details and fix issues like slow themes and thin pages yourself.
## How long does Shopify SEO take to work?

Most Shopify stores see early movement in 3 to 4 months and clearer results in 6 to 12 months. It depends on your store's age, your competition and how much it needs fixing. Technical fixes can help sooner, while content and links take longer to build.
## How often should I review my Shopify SEO checklist?

Check the key numbers in Google Search Console and GA4 once a month. Do a full review every three to six months, or after big changes like a new theme, a migration or a large product launch. New products should be optimised as soon as you add them.
## Do I need an app for Shopify SEO?

No, you can do the basics without one, because Shopify lets you edit titles, descriptions, alt text and redirects. Apps can save time on tasks like bulk edits, image compression or schema. Just don't install more than you need, since each app can slow your store down.
## Can Shopify SEO increase sales?

SEO can help attract people who are actively searching for products like yours. Optimized product and collection pages can make it easier for potential customers to discover and evaluate your products. However, increased traffic doesn't automatically mean increased sales. Product quality, pricing, customer experience, and checkout performance also influence purchasing decisions.
